lenses.title: Best for Aura of Intelligence
lenses.blurb: Human-centred, privacy-first personal AI, cognitive architecture and personal digital twins.

lenses.title: Aura Genesis Protocol
lenses.blurb: A proposed sixty-day process for harmonising and socialising a personal Aura with body and mind, using two hours of daily, single-participant HBOT self-reflection. An Aura can also be created and developed independently of Genesis.
lenses.stage: Published process and research design; no validated clinical programme or participant study is established.
questions: What scientific question, outcome measures and participant consent process would be tested?
Who is the qualified research or clinical lead, and which eligible institution would administer funding?
Which ethics, HBOT operating, privacy and participant-review requirements apply to the actual study?
lenses.funding_note: The research routes below require a defined scientific question, eligible host and researcher qualifications. Their current call and applicant rules must be checked.

lenses.title: Aura Geode
lenses.blurb: The proposed single-person seated chamber and active self-reflection workspace. Hardware development is separate from the Genesis process: conventional HBOT retrofit, geopolymer, crystalline or blended materials, and a future integrated crystalline-compute pathway.
lenses.stage: Published hardware concepts and engineering requirements. New Geode designs and integrated crystalline compute remain development and research work.
questions: Which hardware pathway and component would be funded, and what prototype or measured evidence exists?
Who would lead the engineering review and provide the actual test facility and emergency-egress evidence?
Which applicant entity, IP permissions, maturity level and co-funding are required? Do open-licensing conditions fit the retained licence?
lenses.funding_note: CSIRO Kick-Start requires an eligible Australian entity and cash match for genuine research. Astera has open-first research conditions. EIC requires an eligible applicant and demonstrated technology maturity. Match the specific work package and evidence to the call.

lenses.title: Straddie Disaster Kiosks
lenses.blurb: A proposed Australian community-resilience node, starting on Minjerribah: rugged local-compute kiosks and simpler everyday notice screens, with saved information, sensors, backup power and offline capability. Wider Australian adaptation is an ambition; the public source currently scopes an island concept.
lenses.stage: Public planning pages and pitch material. No operational kiosk network, venue agreement or emergency-warning service is established.
funding_types: Paid pilots where a buyer and procurement route are confirmed
questions: Who would own and maintain the pilot, and which venue has agreed to host it?
Who approves public information, keeps official emergency sources current and manages privacy and corrections?
Does the call accept an individual or require a council, incorporated organisation, research host or auspice? What power, connectivity and electrical-review evidence is needed?
lenses.funding_note: FRRR requires an eligible community organisation or auspice and confirmed location fit. Awesome Foundation is a small community-test lead, subject to chapter fit. A microgrant would not establish funding for the full kiosk or a national rollout.
